text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Employer and employee representatives have both criticised the idea of enforcing collective agreements on more flexible working hours. Chancellor Viktor Klima and Vice Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel expect an agreement this month.
- Social Affairs ministry plans extend part time work in an initiative against rising unemployment.
- An Austrian U.N. observer held hostage by Tajik rebels has been released.
- Klima plans to use managers in special teams on export and technology to boost the economy.
- Car engineer Steyr-Daimler-Puch will produce fewer jeeps for Chrysler in southern Austria due to low demand. Employees will be shifted to Eurostar Steyr's joint-venture with Chrysler.
- Austria's municipalities are ready for Maastricht.
- Austria is too slow in liberalising its telecoms market, the industry says.
- Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt will now be checked by the European Union with a three-week delay.
DIE PRESSE
- Science Minister Caspar Einem wants to increase the number of academics in Austria.
- Austria's construction industry wants to have the possibility of a 50-hour week as the cold winter has proved to be a job-killer.
- Researchers say the retail industry is not making the most of longer shop opening hours, introduced at the start of the year.
KURIER
- The government is pushing the social partners (employers and unions) to come to an agreement on more flexible workhours and is proposing an arbitration board on the issue.
- Austria's federal railways OeBB would have to pay 620 million schillings per year, should the constitutional court come to the conclusion that its exemption from communal taxes is illegal.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- There are 1,000 petrol stations too many in Austria. The closing down of petrol stations will be supported by an 80 million schilling fund financed by oil companies OMV, Shell, BP, Esso and Agip.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- GiroCredit's supervisory board chief Rene Alfons Haiden wants to sell Vienna city's stake in the bank for 415 schillings per share. A decision on who will buy it is expected by June.
